title: Evaluating argumentation graphs as global explainable surrogate models for dense neural networks and their comparison with decision trees
core_idea: Automatically extract rules (arguments) from trained dense neural networks and identify conflicts between them (attacks), integrate arguments and attacks into directed argumentation frameworks, evaluate arguments' dialectical status with formal semantics, and aggregate those statuses to produce surrogate explanations corresponding to the black-box model's target classes.
tldr: Use computational argumentation to create global, rule-based surrogate models for dense neural networks by extracting arguments and their conflicts into argumentation graphs whose semantics yield class-level explanations; these graphs are empirically evaluated and compared with decision-tree surrogates.
